ordered_attempts.student_response: We see the Sun early because clouds act as mirrors and reflect the Sun over the curvature.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-EYE-006: Horizon Straight-Line Geometric Fallacy

topic: Electricity: Electric Potential Difference vs Electric Current

ordered_attempts.stem: A student says: 'In this circuit, 12 volts of electricity is flowing through the 4-ohm resistor.' What conceptual error has the student made?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Voltage flows through the resistor and gets consumed just like water pressure flows through a pipe.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-004: Voltage-Current Conflation / Voltage as Flowing Entity

ordered_attempts.stem: Explain the fundamental operational difference between electric current and potential difference in a circuit.
ordered_attempts.student_response: There is no error; voltage and current are two names for the same flowing electricity.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-004: Voltage-Current Conflation / Voltage as Flowing Entity

topic: Electricity: Factors on which the Resistance of a Conductor Depends (Resistivity)

ordered_attempts.stem: A cylindrical copper wire of resistance R and resistivity rho is cut into two equal halves. What are the resistance and resistivity of each half?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Both resistance and resistivity are halved (R' = R/2 and rho' = rho/2) because cutting the wire cuts everything in half.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-007: Resistivity Dimensional Dependence Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: A wire of length L and uniform cross-section A has resistivity rho. If the wire is stretched to double its length, how does its resistivity change?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Resistivity doubles when length doubles because rho = R * A / L.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-007: Resistivity Dimensional Dependence Fallacy

topic: Electricity: Short Circuit and Parallel Branch Current Distribution

ordered_attempts.stem: A lighted bulb is connected to a battery. A thick copper wire of negligible resistance is now connected directly across the two terminals of the bulb. What happens to the bulb?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The bulb stays on at half brightness because parallel branches always split the current equally.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-008: Zero-Resistance Short Circuit Current Sharing Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: In a circuit with a bulb glowing brightly, an ideal conducting wire (R = 0) is connected in parallel with the bulb. Does the bulb remain lit?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The bulb glows brighter because adding an extra wire provides an easier path for energy to reach it.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-008: Zero-Resistance Short Circuit Current Sharing Fallacy

topic: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current: Magnetic vs Non-Magnetic Materials

ordered_attempts.stem: A student brings a strong permanent bar magnet near a clean sheet of pure copper. Will the copper sheet be attracted to the magnet?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Yes, copper is strongly attracted because copper is a metal and magnets attract all metals.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-002: Universal Metallic Magnetism Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Can an electromagnet or permanent bar magnet be used in a scrap yard to separate aluminum cans from iron scrap? Explain why or why not.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Copper is a great conductor of electricity, so it naturally attracts magnetic fields strongly.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-002: Universal Metallic Magnetism Fallacy

topic: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor in a Magnetic Field

ordered_attempts.stem: A straight wire carrying current is placed inside a uniform magnetic field. Can the magnetic force on the wire ever be in the same direction as the magnetic field lines?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The magnetic force pushes the wire directly along the magnetic field lines towards the North.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: A magnetic field points horizontally towards the North. An electric current flows horizontally towards the East. In which direction does the magnetic force act?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Magnetic force always pulls objects in the same direction that the magnetic field is pointing.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy

topic: Motion: Describing Motion: Distance and Displacement

ordered_attempts.stem: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of radius 7 m in 40 seconds. What are the total distance covered and the net displacement at the end of the round?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Both distance and displacement are 44 m because distance and displacement are the same thing.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MOT-003: Distance Equals Displacement Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: A farmer moves along the boundary of a square field of side 10 m and returns to his starting corner. What is the magnitude of his displacement?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Displacement cannot be zero because the athlete ran hard for 44 meters.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MOT-003: Distance Equals Displacement Fallacy

topic: Motion: Acceleration: Sign of Acceleration and Direction of Motion

ordered_attempts.stem: A car travels towards the West (chosen as negative direction) with velocity -15 m/s and has an acceleration of -3 m/s^2. Is the car speeding up or slowing down?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The car is slowing down because acceleration is negative (-3 m/s^2), and negative acceleration always means braking.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MOT-004: Negative Acceleration Equals Deceleration Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Does a negative acceleration always mean an object is slowing down? Explain using an example of motion along a chosen coordinate axis.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Negative acceleration is deceleration by definition, so the car must be coming to a stop.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MOT-004: Negative Acceleration Equals Deceleration Fallacy

topic: Motion: Average Speed for Equal Distance Intervals

ordered_attempts.stem: A car travels from town A to town B at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns from B to A along the same route at 40 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Average speed is (60 + 40) / 2 = 50 km/h because you simply take the average of the two numbers.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MOT-005: Average Speed Arithmetic Mean Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: A student walks to school at 4 km/h and runs back home along the same path at 6 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Average speed = (4 + 6) / 2 = 5 km/h, just add them and divide by 2.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MOT-005: Average Speed Arithmetic Mean Fallacy

topic: Gravitation: Mass and Weight

ordered_attempts.stem: An astronaut has a mass of 60 kg on Earth. What will be the astronaut's mass and weight on the surface of the Moon, where acceleration due to gravity is 1/6th of Earth's (g_moon = 1.63 m/s^2)?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The astronaut's mass on the Moon is 10 kg because mass becomes 1/6th on the Moon (60 / 6 = 10 kg).
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-FOR-003: Mass-Weight Equivalence Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: A rock weighs 30 N on Earth. What is its mass on Earth and what will be its mass on the Moon?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Mass drops to 10 kg because there is less gravity to hold the mass together.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-FOR-003: Mass-Weight Equivalence Fallacy

topic: Gravitation: Universal Law of Gravitation (Inverse Square Dependence)

ordered_attempts.stem: The gravitational force between two identical spheres separated by distance r is 100 N. If the distance between their centers is doubled to 2r, what is the new gravitational force?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The new force is 50 N because doubling the distance cuts the gravitational pull in half (100 / 2 = 50 N).
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-GRAV-002: Inverse Square Distance Linearity Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: How does the gravitational force between two planets change if the distance between them is tripled?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Force is inversely proportional to distance, so 2 times the distance means half the force.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-GRAV-002: Inverse Square Distance Linearity Fallacy

topic: Work and Energy: Kinetic Energy and Velocity Dependence

ordered_attempts.stem: A moving automobile of mass 1000 kg has a kinetic energy of 50,000 J at 10 m/s. If its speed is doubled to 20 m/s, what is its new kinetic energy?
ordered_attempts.student_response: New kinetic energy is 100,000 J because doubling speed doubles kinetic energy (2 * 50,000 = 100,000 J).
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ENG-001: Kinetic Energy Velocity Linearity Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: How does the kinetic energy of a moving runner change if their speed increases by a factor of 3?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Kinetic energy is directly proportional to speed, so 2 times speed means 2 times the energy.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ENG-001: Kinetic Energy Velocity Linearity Fallacy

topic: Work and Energy: Work Done by Centripetal / Gravitational Force in Circular Motion

ordered_attempts.stem: A satellite orbits the Earth in a circular path at a constant speed of 7 km/s. What is the total work done by Earth's gravitational force on the satellite in one complete revolution?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Gravity does huge work to keep the satellite moving around the circle for millions of meters.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-WRK-002: Circular Orbit Gravitational Work Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Does the gravitational force of the Sun do work on the Earth as it moves in its approximately circular orbit?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Work done = F_gravity * 2*pi*r, force times the circumference traveled.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-WRK-002: Circular Orbit Gravitational Work Fallacy

topic: Optics: Half-Lens Remediation

ordered_attempts.stem: Lower half of convex lens covered with black paper. What happens?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Top half of image is missing.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-OPT-001: Half-Lens Blocking Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: PhET simulation: Observe virtual mask covering lower half.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Wait, the full image is still formed, just dimmer!
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: COGNITIVE_CONFLICT_RECONCILED: Full image persists with 50% brightness

ordered_attempts.stem: Near-transfer: cover top 30% of lens.
ordered_attempts.student_response: The complete image remains, but brightness is 70%.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response

topic: Electricity: Current Conservation Remediation

ordered_attempts.stem: Two identical bulbs in series with 6V battery. Compare ammeters.
ordered_attempts.student_response: A1 = 1.2A, A2 = 0.8A because bulb 1 consumes electric current.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-001: Current Attenuation / Consumption Model

ordered_attempts.stem: PhET Simulation: Observe moving electron dots and ammeters in series.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Both ammeters read identical values (0.90A)! Current is conserved.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: COGNITIVE_CONFLICT_RECONCILED: Current is conserved in closed loop

ordered_attempts.stem: Near-transfer: 100-ohm and 20-ohm resistors in series.
ordered_attempts.student_response: I_in = I_out, because in any series circuit electric charge is conserved.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response

topic: Kinematics: Velocity Calculation

ordered_attempts.stem: Runner covers 100 m in 5 s. Speed?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Speed = distance / time = 100 / 5 = 25 m/s (mental arithmetic slip on division).
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CARELESS_CALCULATION_ERROR

ordered_attempts.stem: Car travels 300 m in 15 s. Speed?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Average speed is distance divided by elapsed time: 300 / 15 = 20 m/s.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response
